script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: forgiveness

Begin screenplay.

---

Title: "The Healing Hands"

INT. LIVING ROOM - DAY

JENNIFER, a 40-something woman with a gentle smile, sits on her plush armchair, her hands folded in her lap. Her eyes wander to the PHOTOGRAPH on the mantelpiece - her husband, MARK, with their 15-year-old son, JOHN. They look happy, healthy, and in love.

Jennifer sighs deeply, her gaze returning to the present. JOHN, looking sullen and withdrawn, enters the room.

JOHN: (bitterly) Hey, Mom.

JENNIFER: (concerned) Hey, sweetheart. Is everything okay?

JOHN: (hesitant) No, not really.

INT. KITCHEN - NIGHT

Mark sits at the kitchen table, pouring over financial reports. He frowns, rubbing his temples.

MARK: (to himself) This is getting worse by the day.

The door swings open, and John enters, his face even more troubled than before.

JOHN: Dad, we need to talk.

INT. LIVING ROOM - DAY

Jennifer and John sit on opposite ends of the couch.

JOHN: (frustrated) I can't take this anymore, Mom. I hate coming home to you and Dad fighting all the time.

JENNIFER: (surprised) Fighting? What are you talking about, John?

JOHN: (angrily) You know exactly what I'm talking about!

INT. BEDROOM - NIGHT

Mark lies in bed, staring at the ceiling. His mind races with worry about their finances.

MARK: (to himself) I should have found a better job when I had the chance. Now it's too late.

INT. SCHOOL - DAY

Jennifer sits in a classroom, listening intently as the TEACHER explains their new community service project.

TEACHER: (enthusiastically) This is a wonderful opportunity for the children to learn the value of giving back to their community. I'm counting on all of you to participate wholeheartedly.

INT. COMMUNITY CENTER - DAY

Jennifer and John volunteer at the community center, serving meals to the homeless. They work together, quietly, their previous tension replaced by a newfound understanding.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Mark comes home from work, finding Jennifer and John sitting together, smiling.

MARK: (surprised) What's going on here?

JENNIFER: (smiling) We've been volunteering at the community center together. It's been great for both of us.

MARK: (relieved) I'm glad you're finding happiness somewhere.

INT. COMMUNITY CENTER - DAY

Mark joins Jennifer and John at the community center, helping serve meals to the homeless. He looks around at the grateful faces and realizes the importance of his family.

MARK: (to Jennifer) I'm sorry for the stress I've been putting you and John through. I'll find a way to make things right.

JENNIFER: (forgivingly) It's okay, Mark. We'll get through this together.

INT. LIVING ROOM - DAY

The family sits together on the couch, watching TV, their hands entwined.

FADE OUT.

---

End of screenplay.
